skill.name: brand-assets-setup
skill.description: Set up a complete brand asset pack for a Next.js App Router project, including favicons, app icons, social images, logo files, metadata, and manifest configuration.
skill.summary: Prepare, import, and validate Next.js brand assets for App Router projects.
skill.author: JohnWayneeee

security_audit.summary: Static command, reconnaissance, and network alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, file path examples, placeholder URLs, and manual validation links. Semantic review found two real safety concerns: automatic deletion of a user-provided source folder and importing generated SVG files without sanitization.

remediation.issue: Destructive deletion of the generated assets folder
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic deletion, or require explicit user confirmation after showing the exact resolved path and successful copy summary.

remediation.issue: Generated SVG files are imported without validation
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize SVG files and reject scripts, event handlers, foreignObject content, and external references before adding them to the project.

remediation.issue: Brand asset imports may overwrite existing project files
remediation.suggestion: Show a diff or overwrite plan first, preserve backups of existing files, and ask for confirmation before replacing assets or metadata.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Source Folder Deletion
semantic_findings.description: The guide instructs the agent to delete the user-provided generated assets folder after import. A mistaken path, partial copy, or unexpected folder contents could cause user data loss.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The deletion instruction is explicit and follows a user-supplied folder path workflow. The skill has Bash access, so the instruction could be acted on with destructive file operations.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated SVG Asset Import
semantic_findings.description: The guide copies generated logo.svg and logo-dark.svg files into the project without requiring sanitization. Generated SVG files can contain scripts, event handlers, or external references if later inlined or processed unsafely.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The import of generated SVG assets is explicit, but the exploitability depends on how the target application renders or bundles the SVG files.

content.value_statement: Next.js teams often miss favicon, PWA, and social image requirements. This skill audits the project, prepares exact asset specs, and wires generated files into App Router conventions.
actual_capabilities: Detects app or src/app layout files and existing brand asset files.
Builds a 12-file checklist with sizes, backgrounds, target paths, and status notes.
Produces an image generation prompt for favicons, app icons, social images, and logo files.
Imports generated assets into App Router, public, and shared asset locations.
Updates metadata, viewport, manifest, Open Graph, Twitter, and robots configuration.
Provides validation steps for favicons, social cards, PWA manifest, and Apple icons.
limitations: It is designed for Next.js App Router projects, not Pages Router or non-Next applications.
It requires a user-provided logo and a generated asset folder.
It does not generate images directly; it prepares a prompt for another image tool.
Asset imports can overwrite files unless the user reviews changes before applying them.

use_cases.title: Launch Product Branding
use_cases.description: Create the required favicon, app icon, and social preview assets before a public launch.

use_cases.title: Standardize App Metadata
use_cases.description: Align App Router metadata, manifest settings, and social card behavior with Next.js conventions.

use_cases.title: Package Designer Handoff
use_cases.description: Turn a logo and color palette into precise file requirements for developers and image tools.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js App Router project and list which brand asset files already exist, which files are missing, and which colors you detect.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Asset Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the complete brand asset generation prompt for this project using the detected brand colors, project name, and logo requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Import Generated Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Import the generated brand asset folder into the correct App Router and public locations, then show the files changed before deleting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Repair Brand Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the Next.js metadata, viewport, manifest, Open Graph, Twitter, and next/image logo usage. Fix inconsistencies and explain each change.

output_examples.input: A Next.js App Router project has a logo but no favicon or social preview images.
output: A checklist shows all required brand assets, their dimensions, backgrounds, target locations, and missing status.
A ready-to-use image generation prompt describes the complete 12-file asset pack.

output_examples.input: A generated brand asset folder is ready for import.
output_examples.output: The assets are placed in the expected App Router, public, and shared asset locations, with changed files summarized for review.

output_examples.input: The project has existing metadata and PWA settings.
output_examples.output: Metadata, manifest values, social card settings, and validation steps are aligned with the detected brand colors and domain.

best_practices: Review the checklist and brand colors before generating image assets.
Keep the original asset folder until browser, social preview, and PWA validation are complete.
Confirm the production domain before changing metadataBase, Open Graph URL, or manifest values.
anti_patterns: Do not import assets from an unclear or untrusted folder path.
Do not overwrite existing brand files without a backup or visible diff.
Do not publish generated SVG files before checking for scripts or external references.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images itself?
faq.answer: No. It prepares exact requirements and a prompt for an external image generation tool.

faq.question: Which projects does it support best?
faq.answer: It supports Next.js App Router projects that use app or src/app directory structures.

faq.question: Can it update existing brand assets?
faq.answer: Yes. It can detect existing files and guide replacement, but users should review changes first.

faq.question: Does it configure social preview images?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Open Graph and Twitter image files and related metadata guidance.

faq.question: Can it set up PWA icons?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers 192 pixel, 512 pixel, and maskable icon assets plus manifest references.

faq.question: What should users review before publishing?
faq.answer: Users should verify the favicon, social previews, manifest icons, brand colors, and any generated SVG files.
